# Model and source

```{r model-meta}
ui <- rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Williams_2026_cabozantinib"))
```

* Citation: `r ui$reference`
* Article: <https://doi.org/10.1111/cts.70738>
* Supplementary Material (NONMEM `$PK` block, Tables S1-S4, Figures S1-S6):
  published with the article.

Williams et al. (2026) updated the cabozantinib population PK model by adding
the phase 1b COSMIC-021 study, in which cabozantinib was given alone or with
atezolizumab to patients with castration-resistant prostate cancer (CRPC) and
other solid tumors. The aim was to estimate covariate effects more precisely
from the larger dataset and to support exposure-response analyses in CRPC. The
earlier transit-compartment absorption model was replaced with a faster-running
dual-phase absorption model.

# Population

The final model was fitted to 7513 quantifiable cabozantinib concentrations
from 2757 participants in 8 studies (Table 1; Supplementary Tables S1-S3): 63
healthy volunteers given single 20, 40 or 60 mg tablet doses (XL184-020), and
patients with CRPC (31.8%), renal cell carcinoma (26.4%), hepatocellular
carcinoma (17.5%), differentiated thyroid cancer (5.3%) and, in COSMIC-021
only, non-small cell lung cancer, urothelial carcinoma and six other tumor
types. Median age was 66 years (range 19-95) and median weight 77.7 kg
(35.0-191); 21.4% were female and 74.9% White. Patients took 20, 40 or 60 mg
once daily, and 770 (27.9%) also received atezolizumab 1200 mg IV every 3
weeks.

```{r population}
str(ui$population)
```

# Model structure

Disposition is two-compartment with linear elimination. Each tablet dose is
split between two parallel inputs (Results, "Base PopPK Model"; Supplementary
Figure S3):

* a fraction `F1 = 0.708` is released into a gut depot by a zero-order process
  lasting `D1 = 0.385 h` after a lag of `ALAG1 = 0.359 h`, and is then absorbed
  first-order (`Ka = 0.826 /h`) into the central compartment;
* the remaining `1 - F1 = 0.292` enters the central compartment directly by a
  zero-order input lasting `D2 = 5.94 h` after a long lag of `ALAG2 = 22.2 h`.

The second input produces the second concentration peak about a day after each
dose. All six absorption parameters were estimated from the healthy-volunteer
study XL184-020 alone and then fixed while the patient data were added.

An event table for this model therefore needs **two** dose records per
administration, with the same `amt` and `rate = -2` (modelled duration): one on
`depot` and one on `central`. The model's `f()`, `alag()` and `dur()` split
and time the two parts, as NONMEM's `F1`/`F2`, `ALAG1`/`ALAG2` and `D1`/`D2`
do for the ADVAN4 depot and central compartments.

```{r structure}
cat(paste(deparse(ui$model), collapse = "\n"))
```

# Source trace

Every `ini()` entry in `inst/modeldb/specificDrugs/Williams_2026_cabozantinib.R`
carries an in-file comment naming its origin. "CS" is the NONMEM code in the
Supplementary Material.

| Parameter | Value | Source location |
|-----------|-------|-----------------|
| `lcl` | CL/F = 2.06 L/h | Table 2; CS `CL = TVCL*EXP(ETA(1))*(BWT/78)**THETA(15)` |
| `lvc` | V2/F = 103 L | Table 2; CS `V2 = TVV2*EXP(ETA(2))*(BWT/78)**THETA(16)` |
| `lq` | Q/F = 19.3 L/h | Table 2; CS `Q = TVQ` |
| `lvp` | V3/F = 192 L | Table 2; CS `V3 = TVV3*EXP(ETA(3))*(BWT/78)**THETA(16)` |
| `lka` | Ka = 0.826 /h (fixed) | Table 2; CS `KA = THETA(5)*EXP(ETA(4)*HV)` |
| `ltlag` | ALAG1 = 0.359 h (fixed) | Table 2; CS `ALAG1 = THETA(6)` |
| `ld1` | D1 = 0.385 h (fixed) | Table 2; CS `D1 = THETA(7)*EXP(ETA(5)*HV)` |
| `ltlag2` | ALAG2 = 22.2 h (fixed) | Table 2; CS `ALAG2 = THETA(8)` |
| `ld2` | D2 = 5.94 h (fixed) | Table 2; CS `D2 = THETA(9)` |
| `logitffo` | logit(F1 = 0.708) (fixed) | Table 2; CS `LGF = LOG(THETA(10)/(1-THETA(10)))+ETA(6)*HV`, `F2 = 1-F1` |
| `e_wt_cl` | 0.0885 | Table 2 "Weight on CL/F"; CS `(BWT/78)**THETA(15)` |
| `e_wt_vc_vp` | 1.04 | Table 2 "Weight on V2/F, weight on V3/F"; CS `THETA(16)` on both V2 and V3 |
| `e_sexf_cl` | -0.201 | Table 2 "Sex on CL/F"; CS `IF(SEXN.EQ.1) CLSEXN=(1+THETA(17))` |
| `etalcl`, `etalvc` block | 0.169 / 0.130 / 0.576 | Table 2 omega2 CL/F, V2/F x CL/F, V2/F |
| `etalka` | 0.373 (healthy volunteers only) | Table 2 omega2 Ka; CS `ETA(4)*HV` |
| `etald1` | 1.59 (healthy volunteers only) | Table 2 omega2 D1; CS `ETA(5)*HV` |
| `etalogitffo` | 0.424, logit scale (healthy volunteers only) | Table 2 omega2 F1; CS `ETA(6)*HV` |
| `propSdHealthy`, `addSdHealthy` | 21.7%, 0.351 ng/mL | Table 2 residual error, HV; CS `RUVCV`, `RUVSD` with `HV = 1` |
| `propSdPatient`, `addSdPatient` | 30.2%, 53.7 ng/mL | Table 2 residual error, patient; CS `RUVCV`, `RUVSD` with `HV = 0` |
| Weight reference 78 kg | -- | CS `BWT = 78`; Figure 4 legend |
| `DIS_HEALTHY` | -- | CS `HV = 1` when `POP = 0` |
| Residual form | combined | Supplementary Material equation `y = yhat x (1 + eps2) + eps1` |

# Event-table helper

```{r make-events}
# Two dose records per administration (depot and central, same amt, rate = -2).
# Observations sit on `central`, the ODE state; Cc is computed from it.
make_subjects <- function(cov, dose_mg, n_doses, obs_times) {
  dose_t <- (seq_len(n_doses) - 1) * 24
  one <- bind_rows(
    data.frame(time = rep(dose_t, each = 2), amt = dose_mg, evid = 1L,
               rate = -2, cmt = rep(c("depot", "central"), n_doses)),
    data.frame(time = obs_times, amt = 0, evid = 0L, rate = 0, cmt = "central")
  )
  ev <- cov[rep(seq_len(nrow(cov)), each = nrow(one)), , drop = FALSE]
  ev <- bind_cols(ev, one[rep(seq_len(nrow(one)), nrow(cov)), ])
  arrange(ev, id, time, desc(evid))
}
```

# Single dose in healthy volunteers

Typical-value profiles after one 20, 40 or 60 mg tablet in a 78 kg male
healthy volunteer. The Discussion describes a first peak about 3 h after the
dose and a second rise about 24 h after it (Figure 3, Supplementary Figure S2).

```{r single-dose}
sd_cov <- data.frame(id = 1:3, dose = c(20, 40, 60), WT = 78, SEXF = 0, DIS_HEALTHY = 1)
sd_obs <- sort(unique(c(seq(0, 48, by = 0.25), seq(49, 504, by = 1))))
sd_ev <- bind_rows(lapply(seq_len(nrow(sd_cov)), function(i) {
  make_subjects(sd_cov[i, ], sd_cov$dose[i], 1, sd_obs)
}))
sd_typ <- rxode2::rxSolve(rxode2::zeroRe(ui), sd_ev, returnType = "data.frame",
                          keep = "dose")

ggplot(sd_typ, aes(time, Cc, colour = factor(dose))) +
  geom_line() +
  scale_y_log10() +
  coord_cartesian(xlim = c(0, 504), ylim = c(1, 400)) +
  labs(x = "Time after dose (h)", y = "Cabozantinib (ng/mL)", colour = "Dose (mg)",
       caption = "Typical single-dose profiles; compare Figure 3 of Williams 2026.")
```

```{r single-dose-shape}
p60 <- filter(sd_typ, dose == 60)
tmax_first <- p60$time[which.max(p60$Cc[p60$time <= 12])]
c20 <- p60$Cc[p60$time == 20]
second <- filter(p60, time >= 20, time <= 48)
tmax_second <- second$time[which.max(second$Cc)]
c(tmax_first = tmax_first, tmax_second = tmax_second)
# Deterministic typical-value solve: the first peak sits near 3 h and the
# second input lifts concentrations again after the 22.2 h lag.
stopifnot(
  tmax_first >= 2, tmax_first <= 4,
  tmax_second > 24, tmax_second < 32,
  max(second$Cc) > 1.5 * c20
)
```

## Closed-form checks

With total bioavailability `F1 + F2 = 1`, a single dose gives
`AUC0-inf = Dose / (CL/F)`, whatever the absorption parameters. The terminal
half-life follows from the disposition parameters alone; the paper reports
104 h.

```{r closed-form}
cl <- 2.06; vc <- 103; q <- 19.3; vp <- 192
k10 <- cl / vc; k12 <- q / vc; k21 <- q / vp
s <- k10 + k12 + k21
beta <- 0.5 * (s - sqrt(s^2 - 4 * k10 * k21))
t_half <- log(2) / beta
t_half

trap <- function(t, y) sum(diff(t) * (head(y, -1) + tail(y, -1)) / 2)
auc_cf <- sd_typ |>
  group_by(dose) |>
  summarise(auc_sim = trap(time, Cc) + last(Cc) / beta, .groups = "drop") |>
  mutate(auc_exact = dose * 1000 / cl,
         pct_diff = 100 * (auc_sim - auc_exact) / auc_exact)
auc_cf |>
  rename("Dose (mg)" = dose, "Simulated AUC0-inf (ng*h/mL)" = auc_sim,
         "Dose / (CL/F) (ng*h/mL)" = auc_exact, "% diff" = pct_diff) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = c(0, 0, 0, 2))

# Same parameters on both sides: the gap is trapezoidal error only.
stopifnot(
  abs(t_half - 104) < 1,
  max(abs(auc_cf$pct_diff)) < 1
)
```

# Covariate effects at steady state (Figure 4)

Figure 4 shows steady-state Cmin, Cmax and Cavg for a 53 kg and a 108 kg
patient (5th and 95th weight percentiles) and for a female patient, relative to
a 78 kg male patient on 60 mg once daily. The maintainers digitised the plotted
ratios. The typical-value model evaluated over the 24 h interval after 30 daily
doses (the same 30-day horizon as Supplementary Table S4) reproduces them.

```{r figure4}
f4_cov <- data.frame(id = 1:4, label = c("Reference", "Weight 53 kg", "Weight 108 kg", "Female"),
                     WT = c(78, 53, 108, 78), SEXF = c(0, 0, 0, 1), DIS_HEALTHY = 0)
f4_ev <- make_subjects(f4_cov, 60, 30, seq(696, 720, by = 0.25))
f4 <- rxode2::rxSolve(rxode2::zeroRe(ui), f4_ev, returnType = "data.frame", keep = "label") |>
  group_by(label) |>
  summarise(Cmin = min(Cc), Cmax = max(Cc), Cavg = trap(time, Cc) / 24, .groups = "drop")
ref <- filter(f4, label == "Reference")
f4_ratio <- f4 |>
  filter(label != "Reference") |>
  transmute(label, Cmin = Cmin / ref$Cmin, Cmax = Cmax / ref$Cmax, Cavg = Cavg / ref$Cavg) |>
  pivot_longer(-label, names_to = "metric", values_to = "simulated")

# Digitised from Williams 2026 Figure 4 (point estimates)
f4_pub <- tibble::tribble(
  ~label,          ~metric, ~published,
  "Weight 53 kg",  "Cmin",  1.028,
  "Weight 108 kg", "Cmin",  0.958,
  "Female",        "Cmin",  1.256,
  "Weight 53 kg",  "Cmax",  1.083,
  "Weight 108 kg", "Cmax",  0.917,
  "Female",        "Cmax",  1.198,
  "Weight 53 kg",  "Cavg",  1.044,
  "Weight 108 kg", "Cavg",  0.948,
  "Female",        "Cavg",  1.236
)
f4_cmp <- inner_join(f4_ratio, f4_pub, by = c("label", "metric")) |>
  mutate(difference = simulated - published)
f4_cmp |>
  rename("Covariate" = label, "Metric" = metric, "Simulated ratio" = simulated,
         "Figure 4 ratio" = published, "Difference" = difference) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 3, caption = "Replicates Figure 4 of Williams 2026.")

# Deterministic: typical values on both sides; digitisation precision is about
# 0.005 (one pixel), so 0.015 still fails for any wrong exponent or sex effect.
stopifnot(nrow(f4_cmp) == 9, max(abs(f4_cmp$difference)) < 0.015)
```

At true steady state the ratios would be slightly larger in magnitude (for
example Cavg 1/(1 - 0.201) = 1.25 for females, 0.972 for 108 kg). After 30
days, the accumulation phase still differs slightly between subjects with
different clearance and volume (terminal half-life about 104 h), and the
figure includes that difference.

# Steady-state exposure by tumor type (Supplementary Table S4)

Supplementary Table S4 gives post hoc steady-state Cavg, Cmax and Cmin after
30 days of treatment. Virtual cohorts of 200 per arm are simulated for four of
its rows, using the sex split and median weight of the matching study from
Supplementary Table S3: RCC 40 mg (CA2099ER), RCC 60 mg (XL184-308), CRPC
60 mg (XL184-307) and healthy volunteers at 60 mg (XL184-020).

```{r cohort}
set.seed(20261008)
rxode2::rxSetSeed(20261008)
n_per_arm <- 200
arms <- tibble::tribble(
  ~treatment,    ~dose, ~female, ~wt_med, ~wt_lo, ~wt_hi, ~hv,
  "RCC 40 mg",      40,  0.231,    80.2,   36.0,  160,    0,
  "RCC 60 mg",      60,  0.223,    79.5,   48.1,  162,    0,
  "CRPC 60 mg",     60,  0,        82.0,   46.7,  161,    0,
  "HV 60 mg",       60,  0.476,    76.5,   58.1,  114,    1
)
ss_obs <- seq(696, 720, by = 0.5)
ss_ev <- bind_rows(lapply(seq_len(nrow(arms)), function(i) {
  a <- arms[i, ]
  cov <- data.frame(
    id = (i - 1) * n_per_arm + seq_len(n_per_arm),
    treatment = a$treatment,
    WT = pmin(pmax(exp(rnorm(n_per_arm, log(a$wt_med), 0.2)), a$wt_lo), a$wt_hi),
    SEXF = rbinom(n_per_arm, 1, a$female),
    DIS_HEALTHY = a$hv
  )
  make_subjects(cov, a$dose, 30, ss_obs)
}))
ss_sim <- rxode2::rxSolve(ui, ss_ev, returnType = "data.frame", keep = "treatment")
stopifnot(!anyNA(ss_sim$Cc), n_distinct(ss_sim$id) == 4 * n_per_arm)
```

`Cc` in the solved output is the individual prediction without residual error,
which is what post hoc exposures describe.

```{r pknca}
conc <- ss_sim |>
  filter(!is.na(Cc)) |>
  select(id, time, Cc, treatment)
doses <- ss_ev |>
  filter(evid == 1, cmt == "depot") |>
  select(id, time, amt, treatment)

conc_obj <- PKNCAconc(conc, Cc ~ time | treatment + id)
dose_obj <- PKNCAdose(doses, amt ~ time | treatment + id)
intervals <- data.frame(start = 696, end = 720, cmax = TRUE, cmin = TRUE, cav = TRUE)
nca <- pk.nca(PKNCAdata(conc_obj, dose_obj, intervals = intervals))
```

```{r nca-compare}
# Supplementary Table S4 medians (ng/mL)
published <- tibble::tribble(
  ~treatment,   ~cav, ~cmax, ~cmin,
  "RCC 40 mg",   879,   996,   807,
  "RCC 60 mg",  1253,  1432,  1146,
  "CRPC 60 mg", 1220,  1391,  1117,
  "HV 60 mg",   1354,  1538,  1252
)
cmp <- nlmixr2lib::ncaComparisonTable(
  simulated = nca,
  reference = published,
  by = "treatment",
  units = c(cav = "ng/mL", cmax = "ng/mL", cmin = "ng/mL"),
  tolerance_pct = 20
)
cmp |>
  rename("Population and dose" = treatment) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "Simulated median steady-state exposure versus Supplementary Table S4 (post hoc medians).")
```

```{r nca-gate}
sim_med <- as.data.frame(nca$result) |>
  filter(PPTESTCD %in% c("cav", "cmax", "cmin")) |>
  group_by(treatment, PPTESTCD) |>
  summarise(sim = median(PPORRES), .groups = "drop")
pub_long <- pivot_longer(published, -treatment, names_to = "PPTESTCD", values_to = "pub")
gate <- inner_join(sim_med, pub_long, by = c("treatment", "PPTESTCD")) |>
  mutate(pct_diff = 100 * (sim - pub) / pub)
# Centre of a 200-subject cohort (CL/F IIV 43% CV, so the median carries
# roughly 4% sampling error) against post hoc medians of the real cohorts.
# A wrong CL/F, dose scaling or unit factor moves every row by tens of percent.
stopifnot(nrow(gate) == 12, abs(median(gate$pct_diff)) < 10, max(abs(gate$pct_diff)) < 20)
```

```{r vpc-plot}
ss_sim |>
  group_by(treatment, time) |>
  summarise(p05 = quantile(Cc, 0.05), p50 = median(Cc), p95 = quantile(Cc, 0.95),
            .groups = "drop") |>
  ggplot(aes(time - 696, p50)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = p05, ymax = p95), alpha = 0.25) +
  geom_line() +
  facet_wrap(~treatment) +
  labs(x = "Time after the 30th dose (h)", y = "Cabozantinib (ng/mL)",
       caption = "Simulated median and 5th-95th percentiles over the 30th dosing interval.")
```

# Assumptions and deviations

* **NONMEM code is incomplete.** The Supplementary Material prints the `$PK`
  block only, up to `S2 = V2/100`; `$THETA`, `$OMEGA`, `$SIGMA` and `$ERROR`
  are not shown. Parameter values come from Table 2, and the residual-error
  form comes from the supplement's equation `y = yhat x (1 + eps2) + eps1`
  with the `RUVCV`/`RUVSD` assignments, read as standard deviations (Table 2
  reports them as % and ng/mL). Independent proportional and additive errors
  add their variances, which is nlmixr2's default `combined2` form.
* **No IIV on V3/F.** The `$PK` code multiplies V3 by `EXP(ETA(3))`, but Table 2
  lists no variance for it and the Results list the IIV terms as CL/F, V2/F,
  Ka, D1 and F1 only. `ETA(3)` is taken to have been fixed to zero, and the
  model carries no eta on `vp`.
* **Scale factor.** The code sets `S2 = V2/100`. With doses in mg and
  concentrations in ng/mL the factor would be `V2/1000`. The data-file dose
  units are not reported. The model uses mg and ng/mL
  (`Cc = central / vc * 1000`). This is confirmed by mass balance: CL/F = 2.06
  L/h at 60 mg/day gives Cavg = 1214 ng/mL, in line with the Supplementary
  Table S4 medians (1062-1404 ng/mL), and by the Figure 4 replication above.
* **Reported CV% for some variances.** Table 2 gives CV% next to each omega2
  using `CV = sqrt(exp(omega2) - 1)`. That reproduces the CL/F (42.9%) and D1
  (198%) entries but not Ka (0.373 gives 67.2%, table 65.5%), V2/F (0.576
  gives 88.3%, table 89.4%) or F1 (0.424 gives 72.7%, table 74.4%). The
  variances are used as printed.
* **Absorption IIV applies to healthy volunteers only.** This follows the
  code (`ETA(4)*HV`, `ETA(5)*HV`, `ETA(6)*HV`). For patients
  (`DIS_HEALTHY = 0`), Ka, D1 and F1 take their typical values.
* **Sex coding.** `SEXN = 1` is read as female, because the Results report
  about 20% lower CL/F in females and the estimate is -0.201.
* **Virtual cohorts.** Body weight is drawn log-normally around each study's
  median from Supplementary Table S3 (log-SD 0.2) and truncated to the study's
  range; sex is drawn from the study's female fraction. Supplementary Table S4
  uses the actual patients' post hoc parameters, so only the centre of each
  distribution is compared.
* **Figure 4 digitisation.** The ratios were read from the published PNG at
  about 0.005 per pixel. The figure's error bars reflect parameter uncertainty
  and are not reproduced.
* **Covariates screened but not retained** (age, race, AST, ALT, total
  bilirubin, creatinine, hepatic function, tumor type and atezolizumab
  co-treatment) are documented in the model's `covariatesDataExcluded`
  metadata.
* **No erratum** for this article was found when the maintainers checked on
  2026-11-18.
